original_question: Determine whether isotropic singularities are typical in modified theories of gravity, rather than being a special feature of only restricted models.
target_in_paper: Problem P17 in Section 5.2, subsection Isotropic singularity: Are isotropic singularities typical in modified theories of gravity.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact core problem almost verbatim: it asks whether isotropic singularities are typical in modified theories of gravity, which is precisely the content of Problem P17. Your added contrast with restricted models is also faithful to the nearby context, because the paper motivates P17 by listing only a few special positive examples in higher-order curvature, Gauss-Bonnet, and quadratic-Ricci settings.
missing_details: The paper places the problem in cosmology, specifically near the initial cosmological singularity; it is not about arbitrary singularities in all gravitational settings.
The nearby definition identifies isotropic singularities with conformal singularities, namely singularities at which the conformal structure remains regular.
The motivation is Penrose's Weyl curvature hypothesis: the initial singularity should have Weyl curvature tending to zero or at least remaining bounded.
The paper frames the question as one about isotropization close to the cosmological singularity.
The paper does not specify any one modified theory; the scope is alternative, modified theories of gravity in general.
The word typical is left informal in the paper; no topology, measure, perturbation class, or exact notion of genericity/stability is fixed.
No dimension, matter content, equation-of-state range, or symmetry class is imposed in Problem P17 itself; those appear only in illustrative examples after the problem statement.

The nearby examples are evidence and motivation, not extra hypotheses: higher-order curvature corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, Gauss-Bonnet gravity in a higher-dimensional anisotropic universe with a perfect fluid, and quadratic Ricci-curvature corrections.
refined_question: In the cosmological setting of initial singularities, determine whether isotropic singularities—equivalently, conformal singularities for which the conformal structure remains regular at the singularity, in the sense motivated by Penrose's Weyl-curvature hypothesis—are typical in alternative modified theories of gravity, rather than occurring only in special exact models such as the known higher-order curvature, Gauss-Bonnet, or quadratic-Ricci examples.
equivalent_formulation: Determine whether cosmological initial singularities with regular conformal structure are typical in modified theories of gravity.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Problem P17 exactly. The surrounding discussion first defines the relevant notion of isotropic singularity through regularity of the conformal structure and links it to Penrose's Weyl-curvature hypothesis, then states P17, and immediately explains why the question arises by citing special model results in higher-order curvature, Gauss-Bonnet, and quadratic-Ricci gravity. The refined version therefore keeps the official scope of P17, adds only the nearby definitional context needed to make the question stand alone, and avoids introducing a more specific modified-gravity class or a stronger formal notion of genericity than the paper itself states.
